lines.text: decision for God has to be consummated ever afresh when we
are confronted by Him in the actualities of living and His
call strikes us. Again and again it is the decisive now on
which everything turns. By His living encounters with us
God puts us to the test. The heart of the matter is to hold
ourselves in readiness for His call, which requires us to be
inwardly detached from all that claims our attention, from
work and care, from sorrow and joy, and to see that nothing
claims and absorbs us wholly, with the consequence that we
become blind to His confrontation and deaf to His call.
CIV
This brings us to the main point. To be ready for God's call
means just this—to be prepared to live in the conviction
that our life of earthly work with its cares and projects, its
sorrows and joys, is not the ultimate reality. What then is the
essence of God's invitation? It is surely the call to a higher
life, to a future life, to a life that lies beyond this world.
It is the call to free ourselves from this world and to become
centred in God's world
No doubt when things are going badly with us here, when
we feel acutely the oppressiveness of our wretched and dis-
tressing fate, we long to soar beyond it all and we eagerly
listen to this call which invites us to another world where
there is no more pain and sorrow. But God's call demands
more than this. It demands that in good as in bad times we
should be deeply aware that this our world can give us no
final satisfaction, can bestow on us no true fullness of life.
God's call faces us with the decision between our world and
His world, between the present and the future, between the
here and now and the beyond. Do we really want the reality
of God or do we in fact want our world and God only oc-
casionally for the purpose of transfiguring and enhancing
our world? Is it the fact that as far as we are concerned, what
we plan and do here, the structures of life which we carve
out and build with all the trouble and care involved, what
